script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'hashcards-explore',
  description: 'Exhaustively probe the hashcards binary behavior across all surfaces',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Explore' },
  ],
}

const COMMON = [
  'You are reverse-engineering a compiled binary by BEHAVIORAL OBSERVATION ONLY.',
  '',
  'Binary: /workspace/executable  (a spaced-repetition CLI called "hashcards", version 0.3.0)',
  'Docs: /workspace/README.md ; example collection: /tmp/explore/_example_master (copy it, never modify the master)',
  '',
  'HARD RULES (violating these fails the whole task):',
  '- NEVER decompile, disassemble, or inspect the binary bytes (no objdump, nm, strings, readelf, ghidra, gdb, hexdump on /workspace/executable).',
  '- NEVER use strace/ltrace/perf or any tracing on /workspace/executable.',
  '- NEVER search the internet or any package registry for the project source code. You have no network anyway.',
  '- ONLY run the binary with CLI args / HTTP requests and observe stdout, stderr, exit codes, files it writes, and HTTP responses.',
  '',
  'Environment: python3 (3.10, has sqlite3 module), curl, no network. Use python3 to inspect the hashcards.db SQLite file.',
  '',
  'Working discipline:',
  '- Work ONLY inside your own scratch dir (mkdir -p it).',
  '- Write detailed findings to your findings file as you go. Be exhaustive and BYTE-EXACT: paste literal expected output, exact error strings, exact exit codes.',
  '- Save large artifacts (full HTML/CSS/JS/JSON dumps) as separate files in a sibling directory and reference them.',
  '- Your final returned text must be a dense, complete summary of the RULES you inferred (not a narration of what you tried). Someone must be able to reimplement from it.',
  '- Prefer many small experiments. Test edge cases aggressively. When you see a rule, try to break it.',
  '',
].join('\n')

phase('Explore')

const AREAS = [
  {
    key: 'cli-surface',
    prompt: [
      'AREA: CLI surface / argument parsing (the binary uses a Rust clap-style parser).',
      '',
      'Capture BYTE-EXACT text for:',
      '- the binary with no args; --help; -h; --version; -V',
      '- every subcommand with -h AND with --help (they differ: -h is the short summary, --help the long one): drill, check, stats, orphans, orphans list, orphans delete, export',
      '- the help subcommand: help / help drill / help orphans / help orphans list / help help',
      '- error cases: unknown subcommand, unknown flag, missing flag value, invalid value for --answer-controls / --format / --open-browser / --bury-siblings, non-numeric --port / --card-limit / --new-card-limit, out-of-range port (99999, -1, 0), too many positional args, bare -- handling, flag abbreviation (does --por 1 work?), equals-sign vs space form.',
      '- exit codes for every case, and whether output goes to stdout or stderr.',
      '- directory argument handling for check/stats/export/drill: nonexistent dir, a file instead of a dir, unreadable dir, empty dir, relative vs absolute path, trailing slash, dot and dot-dot, path with spaces. Record the EXACT error text and exit code.',
      'Write everything with fenced literal blocks.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'collection-discovery',
    prompt: [
      'AREA: How a collection directory is scanned.',
      '',
      'Determine precisely:',
      '- Which files are treated as decks? extension matching (.md, .MD, .markdown, .txt)? case sensitivity?',
      '- Are subdirectories recursed into? If so, how is deckName derived for a nested file (e.g. sub/dir/Foo.md)? Test deep nesting.',
      '- Are hidden files/dirs (starting with a dot) skipped? Is a .git dir skipped? Is a hidden dir containing .md files skipped?',
      '- Are symlinks followed (file symlinks and dir symlinks)? What about broken symlinks?',
      '- Is hashcards.db itself skipped? What about macros.tex?',
      '- Ordering: what order are decks/cards processed in? Does export sort cards (by hash? by file?)? Determine the exact sort key by constructing cases.',
      '- Deck name derivation: filename without extension? What about a file named a.b.md? A unicode filename? A file named just .md?',
      '- Where and when is hashcards.db created (which commands create it, in which directory)? Is it created when the collection is empty? For read-only commands like export/stats?',
      '- Empty directory; directory with no .md files; directory containing markdown with no cards.',
      '- Duplicate identical cards across files and within a file: which one survives in export (report the deckName/location kept) and what determines that. Test 3-way duplicates across files named to disambiguate ordering.',
      'Use export (JSON to stdout) as your main observation tool.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'md-parse-basic',
    prompt: [
      'AREA: Markdown deck parsing - BASIC (Q:/A:) cards, and the overall block/card splitting grammar.',
      '',
      'Determine the exact grammar. Test at minimum:',
      '- Marker syntax: "Q:" vs "Q :" vs lowercase "q:" vs "Q>"; is a space required after the colon? "Q:x" vs "Q: x". Leading whitespace/indentation before the marker. Tabs.',
      '- Multi-line questions: does the question continue onto following lines until an A: line? Blank lines inside a question?',
      '- Multi-line answers: where does the answer end (blank line? next Q:/C:? end of file?). Test an answer containing a blank line followed by more text.',
      '- Text before the first card and between cards (prose, headings, HTML comments, YAML frontmatter, horizontal rules) - ignored, or an error?',
      '- Q: with no A:; A: with no Q:; two A: in a row; empty question; empty answer; card at EOF with no trailing newline; CRLF line endings; a UTF-8 BOM.',
      '- Exact trimming rules applied to question and answer text (leading/trailing blank lines, trailing spaces, internal indentation).',
      '- lineStart/lineEnd semantics in the export JSON: 0-based? inclusive/exclusive? Construct cases with prose before/after and blank lines to pin it down EXACTLY and give a formula.',
      '- How cards are separated: is a blank line required between two cards?',
      '- Code fences: is a marker line inside a triple-backtick fence still treated as a marker?',
      '- Does the parser strip carriage returns from content?',
      'Use export and check. Give a precise grammar/algorithm at the end.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'md-parse-cloze',
    prompt: [
      'AREA: Markdown deck parsing - CLOZE (C:) cards.',
      '',
      'The export JSON for a cloze card has content {"cloze": {"text": <text with brackets removed>, "start": N, "end": M}} and a familyHash shared by all clozes of the same text. Prior finding: start/end look like BYTE offsets into the rendered text with an INCLUSIVE end (verify rigorously with multi-byte UTF-8 such as e-acute, em dash, emoji, and with single-character deletions).',
      '',
      'Determine:',
      '- Exact cloze syntax with square brackets. What about an empty pair? Nested brackets? An unclosed bracket? An unopened one? A backslash-escaped bracket?',
      '- Interaction with markdown links and images (bracket-paren syntax) - are those treated as clozes? Test a link inside a cloze card and a cloze inside a link.',
      '- Multi-line clozes; a cloze spanning a line break.',
      '- A C: card with no brackets at all - error, or zero cards?',
      '- How many cards are produced per cloze text (one per bracket) and their ordering in export.',
      '- familyHash: identical for all clozes of the same text? Does it depend on deck/file? Same text in two different files?',
      '- The same bracket content twice in one text - two cards with different offsets?',
      '- lineStart/lineEnd semantics for cloze cards.',
      '- Exact text normalization: is the text trimmed? are the brackets simply removed?',
      '- Mixed Q:/A: and C: in one file, adjacent.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'check-command',
    prompt: [
      'AREA: The check subcommand.',
      '',
      'On a valid collection it prints ok and exits 0 (verify exact bytes and trailing newline).',
      'Find EVERY failure mode and its exact message and exit code. Try to provoke:',
      '- malformed cards (A: without Q:, Q: without A:, unclosed cloze bracket, C: with no clozes, empty card text)',
      '- duplicate cards',
      '- broken media links: an image whose file does not exist; the @/ prefix form; absolute paths; remote URLs; anchors',
      '- broken/invalid LaTeX, unbalanced dollar signs, an undefined macro not in macros.tex',
      '- a macros.tex with bad syntax',
      '- unreadable file, non-UTF8 file, a directory named x.md',
      '- a corrupt/foreign hashcards.db, a hashcards.db that is not a database, a read-only db',
      '- orphan cards in the db (rows whose hash is no longer in any deck) - does check report them?',
      'Also determine: does check create/modify hashcards.db (diff the db before/after with python3 sqlite3)? Does it insert new card rows?',
      'Does check report multiple errors at once or stop at the first? What is the ordering of reported errors?',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'export-json',
    prompt: [
      'AREA: The export subcommand and its full JSON schema.',
      '',
      '- Determine the complete JSON schema: top-level keys, key order, indentation (2 spaces?), trailing newline, pretty printing, how nulls are emitted, camelCase naming.',
      '- Card object fields: hash, familyHash, deckName, location{filePath,lineStart,lineEnd}, content (tagged union basic/cloze), performance. Is filePath absolute or as given? Test with a relative dir arg, an absolute one, and from a different cwd.',
      '- The performance field is null for unreviewed cards. Drill a session and record the populated shape: field names, types, date formats.',
      '- The sessions array: populate it by drilling and record the exact shape.',
      '- --output FILE behavior: file created? overwritten? trailing newline? nonexistent parent dir? Is anything printed to stdout then?',
      '- Sort order of cards (by hash ascending? verify) and of sessions.',
      '- Does export create or modify hashcards.db?',
      '',
      'To create review data drive the drill web UI. Start it with the drill subcommand using --port 8301 --open-browser false. It serves a server-rendered HTML page at / and accepts POSTs to / with form field action (values seen: Undo, Reveal, End, and rating buttons Forgot/Hard/Good/Easy). Use curl -X POST -d action=Reveal etc. Drive several cards, then End, then run export.',
      'Also save a full sample export to your artifacts dir.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'stats-command',
    prompt: [
      'AREA: The stats subcommand (--format html | json).',
      '',
      '- Capture the FULL byte-exact HTML output for: an empty collection, the example collection with no reviews, and a collection with review history. Save each as a file.',
      '- Capture the JSON output for the same cases; determine the complete schema, key order, number formatting (floats: how many decimals?), date formats.',
      '- Figure out what each statistic means and how it is computed (counts by state, due today, retention, interval histogram, reviews per day, forecast?). Derive formulas by constructing collections with known review histories and checking the numbers.',
      '- Is the HTML self-contained (inline CSS)? Does it reference /style.css?',
      '- Trailing newline? Exit code? Does stats create/modify hashcards.db?',
      '',
      'To create review data drive the drill web UI on --port 8302 --open-browser false, then POST to / with form field action = Reveal / Good / Hard / Easy / Forgot / Undo / End. You can ALSO fabricate histories by writing rows directly into hashcards.db with python3 sqlite3 (dates in the past, many reviews) and then running stats - this is a great way to derive formulas.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'orphans',
    prompt: [
      'AREA: The orphans subcommand (list, delete).',
      '',
      '- Definition of an orphan: presumably a row in the sqlite cards table whose card_hash no longer corresponds to any card in the markdown files. Verify.',
      '- orphans list: exact output format (one hash per line? sorted? header? what when there are none?), exit code. Does it take a DIRECTORY argument? Check its --help.',
      '- orphans delete: exact output, what rows it removes (cards only? also reviews? sessions?), exit code, behavior when there are none, any confirmation prompt.',
      '- Behavior when there is no hashcards.db yet. Do these commands create it?',
      '',
      'Set up orphans by drilling some cards (to insert card rows) then editing/removing the markdown, or by inserting rows directly with python3 sqlite3.',
      'Schema: cards(card_hash text primary key, added_at text not null, last_reviewed_at text, stability real, difficulty real, interval_raw real, interval_days integer, due_date text, review_count integer not null) strict; sessions(session_id integer primary key, started_at text not null, ended_at text not null) strict; reviews(review_id integer primary key, session_id integer not null references sessions, card_hash text not null references cards, reviewed_at text not null, grade text not null, stability real not null, difficulty real not null, interval_raw real not null, interval_days integer not null, due_date text not null) strict.',
      'Use port 8303 if you need to drill.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'drill-http',
    prompt: [
      'AREA: The drill web server - HTTP protocol surface and session state machine. Use --port 8304 --open-browser false.',
      '',
      'Determine:',
      '- All routes: GET / , POST / , GET /style.css , /script.js , /katex/katex.css , /katex/katex.js , /katex/mhchem.js , media files (figure out the URL scheme for e.g. test.mp3 and thetempest.webp), unknown paths (404 body and headers), other methods (PUT/DELETE/HEAD/OPTIONS), HTTP/1.0 requests, keep-alive behavior.',
      '- Exact response headers for each (names, order, casing, content-type values, content-length, date, connection, cache-control, etag).',
      '- The POST form: field name(s) and every accepted value. Observed: action=Reveal, Undo, End, and grade buttons Forgot/Hard/Good/Easy. Determine responses (200 with new HTML, or 303 redirect?). Invalid/missing action value. URL-encoding.',
      '- The full state machine: question shown -> Reveal -> answer shown -> grade -> next card -> ... -> no cards left (what does the done page look like?) -> End (final page? does the server shut down? does the process exit and with what code?).',
      '- Undo: how far back can you go? What does it restore? Is it disabled on the first card?',
      '- After End: does the process exit? Does the port close? What does a subsequent request return?',
      '- Card ordering within a session: deterministic or random? Run the same collection twice from a fresh db and compare.',
      '- --card-limit, --new-card-limit, --from-deck, --answer-controls binary, --bury-siblings true/false: how each changes the served HTML and the card set.',
      '- --host binding, --port already in use (error message and exit code), --open-browser true in a headless env.',
      '- The progress bar percentage: derive the formula.',
      '- What is served when the collection has zero due cards at startup?',
      'Save every distinct HTML page byte-exact as files, and write out the state machine.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'drill-render',
    prompt: [
      'AREA: Markdown to HTML rendering used by the drill web UI. Use --port 8305 --open-browser false over a scratch collection you control; change the markdown, restart, re-fetch.',
      '',
      'Determine the exact HTML produced for:',
      '- paragraphs, soft/hard line breaks, headings, bold/italic/strikethrough, inline code, fenced code blocks with and without a language (is a highlight.js class emitted?), blockquotes, ordered/unordered/nested lists, tables (GFM?), task lists, footnotes, autolinks, raw inline HTML, horizontal rules, entity escaping, smart punctuation (are quotes/dashes/ellipses transformed?).',
      '- math: inline single-dollar and display double-dollar - what HTML does the server emit (raw text left for client-side KaTeX, or server-side rendered)? Read /script.js to see how the client renders math and which delimiters it configures.',
      '- The macros.tex file in the collection root: figure out its format (the example contains a line defining a macro named euler) and how macros reach the client (embedded in the HTML? passed to KaTeX?). Test multiple macros, macros with arguments, comments, blank lines.',
      '- images: relative src, the @/ prefix form, remote URLs, missing files. What src does the emitted img tag have? How is the media file served over HTTP?',
      '- audio/video: an image-syntax link to an .mp3 - is it turned into an audio element? Which extensions map to audio/video? Exact HTML.',
      '- cloze cards: how is the deleted span rendered on the question side vs the answer side (span/class)? Capture both.',
      '- The card HTML skeleton and the answer-side variant.',
      'Save byte-exact samples and write out the rules.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'assets',
    prompt: [
      'AREA: Static assets served by the drill server, captured byte-exact. Make a scratch collection with one card, run drill on --port 8306 --open-browser false.',
      '',
      'Download and SAVE these files verbatim into /tmp/findings/assets/ using curl -s -o so bytes are preserved:',
      '- /style.css , /script.js , /katex/katex.css , /katex/katex.js , /katex/mhchem.js',
      '- Probe for additional asset routes the CSS/JS references: parse katex.css for font URLs (e.g. /katex/fonts/KaTeX_Main-Regular.woff2) and fetch every one you find into /tmp/findings/assets/katex/fonts/. Also check /favicon.ico, /robots.txt, and any path referenced from style.css or script.js.',
      'Record each file size and sha256, plus the exact Content-Type header and any caching headers returned.',
      'Then READ style.css and script.js and summarize: the CSS class names used by the app, and exactly what script.js does (keyboard shortcuts, KaTeX rendering options and delimiters, highlight.js invocation, how it reads macros, the card-content opacity reveal).',
      'Report the list of files saved with sizes.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'fsrs-scheduling',
    prompt: [
      'AREA: The spaced-repetition scheduling algorithm (likely FSRS) and the sqlite database writes.',
      '',
      'Schema: cards(card_hash text primary key, added_at text, last_reviewed_at text, stability real, difficulty real, interval_raw real, interval_days integer, due_date text, review_count integer not null); sessions(session_id, started_at, ended_at); reviews(review_id, session_id, card_hash, reviewed_at, grade, stability, difficulty, interval_raw, interval_days, due_date).',
      '',
      'Drive the drill UI to generate reviews on --port 8307 --open-browser false: POST form field action=Reveal then action=Good (or Forgot/Hard/Easy), repeat, then action=End. Then dump the db with python3.',
      '',
      'Determine EXACTLY:',
      '- The text formats of added_at, last_reviewed_at, due_date, started_at, ended_at, reviewed_at (RFC3339? date only? UTC or local? precision?).',
      '- The grade string values stored for each button.',
      '- Initial stability/difficulty for a brand-new card for each of the 4 grades (print full float precision via python repr). These are FSRS w[0..3] for stability and a function of w[4],w[5] for difficulty.',
      '- The update formulas for subsequent reviews. Strategy: fabricate card rows directly in sqlite with chosen stability/difficulty/due_date/last_reviewed_at (including past dates so elapsed days > 0), then drill that card and read the new values. Sweep systematically (stability 0.1,1,5,20,100; difficulty 1,3,5,7,10; elapsed 0,1,5,30) for each grade. Record a table of (S,D,elapsed,grade) -> (S2,D2,interval_raw,interval_days,due_date) as CSV.',
      '- How interval_days derives from interval_raw (rounding? clamping? min 1?) and how due_date derives from interval_days.',
      '- The desired retention (interval_raw as a function of S and retention).',
      '- Whether Forgot resets or uses a lapse formula; whether there is a learning-step / same-session re-queue.',
      '- review_count semantics; when a card row is first inserted (at first review, or at scan time?).',
      '- Are sessions rows written at End only? What are started_at/ended_at?',
      'Be quantitative, dump raw numbers with full precision, and give derived formulas.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
  {
    key: 'drill-selection',
    prompt: [
      'AREA: Which cards get drilled, in what order, and the queue/limits logic. Use --port 8308 --open-browser false. The served HTML contains the deck name in an h1 and the question text, so you can identify each card in sequence. POST action=Reveal then action=Good to advance.',
      '',
      'Determine:',
      '- The candidate set: all cards with due_date <= today, plus new (never reviewed) cards? Verify by fabricating db rows with due dates in the future/past via python3 sqlite3.',
      '- Ordering: random per run or deterministic? Run the same fresh collection twice and compare the sequence. If random, is there grouping (new cards first/last, by deck)?',
      '- --card-limit N: caps total cards? which N are chosen?',
      '- --new-card-limit N: caps how many never-seen cards enter the session; interaction with --card-limit.',
      '- --from-deck NAME: exact matching (case sensitive? full deck name? nonexistent deck - error message and exit code?).',
      '- --bury-siblings true/false: siblings share a familyHash. With burying on, at most one card per family per session? Verify with the example Quotes deck (3 sibling clozes) and Geography.',
      '- After grading Forgot, does the card reappear later in the same session? What about Hard?',
      '- The progress bar width formula: capture the inline width percentage at each step and derive it.',
      '- The session-finished page, and what happens when there are zero cards to drill at startup (exact HTML and stdout).',
      '- Anything printed to stdout/stderr by drill (startup banner, URL, per-review logging, shutdown message) - byte exact.',
    ].join('\n'),
  },
]

const results = await parallel(AREAS.map((a) => () =>
  agent(COMMON + '\n' + a.prompt + '\n\nYour scratch dir is /tmp/explore/' + a.key + '. Write findings to /tmp/findings/' + a.key + '.md and artifacts under /tmp/findings/' + a.key + '/.',
    { label: a.key, phase: 'Explore' })
))

return AREAS.map((a, i) => ({ area: a.key, summary: results[i] }))
